Detect a distributional parameter that starts at a useless stationary point

Source: R/fit.R
dot-flat_start.Rd

A parameter whose intercept has an identically zero score cannot move, and a smooth on it then drifts on a flat surface instead of failing loudly. dskewnorm2's alpha does this at alpha = 0; see fam().

Usage

.flat_start(grad, eval_at, pfull, is_beta, design)

Arguments

grad

Joint gradient at the starting values.

eval_at

Function of a full parameter vector returning the objective.

pfull

The full starting parameter vector.

is_beta

Logical index of the beta entries within pfull.

design

The design object.

Value

A message describing the affected parameters, or NULL.

Details

A zero score is not on its own a problem: an intercept started at its own marginal optimum has one too, and that is exactly where it should be (dnbinom2's mu started at log(mean(y)) has a zero score and fits perfectly). The two are told apart by probing rather than by curvature — perturb the intercept either way and see whether the objective actually falls. A stationary point that can be improved on by stepping away from it is the bad kind.
